title: Tenure, Transfer Counts and Concessions Across the Chain of Lease Term Agreements
content:
Tenure, transfer counts and concession recapture on a Lease Term Agreement are measured across the whole chain of terms on a lease, never on a single term.

## 1. Continuous tenancy

1.1 Continuous tenancy runs from the lease's move-in date through every renewal, transfer and month-to-month conversion term; it resets only when a new lease is signed after the previous lease closed.

1.2 *Measure of tenure.* Tenure is the number of full calendar months of continuous tenancy on the lease, counted from the move-in date of the lease to the evaluation date across the whole chain of its terms — new-lease, renewal, transfer and month-to-month conversion terms alike — from a day number to the same day number of a later month, falling back to the last day of that month when that day number does not exist.

1.3 *Retired clause.* The clause "the loyalty reduction of the renewal increase cap applies when the tenure on the offer date is at least the expiring term program's loyalty tenure" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the loyalty reduction of the renewal increase cap. The program figures it referred to — the loyalty tenure and the loyalty reduction of each term program — remain the program's published values.

## 2. Transfer counts

2.1 Transfers are counted over all terms of the lease, using the trailing transfer count, and compared with the program's allowance of transfers per trailing 365 days.

2.2 *Measure of transfers.* The trailing transfer count is the number of signed transfer requests (requests for a transfer to another apartment home that the resident signed) on any term of the lease whose submission date falls within the trailing 365 calendar days ending on and including the evaluation date.

## 3. Concessions on an early exit

3.1 *Retired clause.* The clause "the unearned concession recaptured on an early exit is computed from the concession of the lease's new-lease term, even when the exit happens under a later term; a concession is never recaptured once the new-lease term has run to its end date" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the unearned months of a concession.

3.2 The measure that retired clause named — the unearned concession, taken from the day after the termination date through the end date of the terminating term, as the total of the rent concession credits posted on the lease ledger for the lease's new-lease term, multiplied by the full months from the termination date to the term end date and divided by the term's months, rounded half up to the cent — belongs to the retired clause.

## Points of judgement

- *Does a renewal restart tenure?* No. Tenure runs across renewal, transfer and month-to-month conversion terms of the same lease.
- *Does a transfer to another apartment home restart tenure?* No; a transfer term is part of the same chain.
- *When does tenure restart?* Only when a new lease is signed after the previous lease closed.
- *Hypothetical.* A lease with a move-in date of 20 May has, on 19 May two years later, 23 full months of tenure; on 20 May it has 24.

superseded_clauses: The loyalty reduction of the renewal increase cap applies when term_msr_tenure_months on the offer date is at least the expiring term program's loyalty_min_tenure_months.

The unearned concession recaptured on an early exit is computed from the concession of the lease's new-lease term (term_msr_unearned_concession), even when the exit happens under a later term; a concession is never recaptured once the new-lease term has run to its term_end_date.
